scope: Every tank request of the accepted prepared v2 fixtures against 2, 3, 4 and 5 copies of the boss that all swing at the tank: 73 requests of one target with a tank assignment, 22 Druid, 19 Warrior, 27 Paladin, 4 Rogue and 1 Mage, which cover the shields, absorbs, item procs, survival cooldowns, explosives, Sulfuras, Eye for an Eye, Retaliation, Blood Craze, Thunder Clap, Last Stand, Stoneform and Shatter Curse variants of the production tanks. Each is exported with the pinned Go engine and run by Go and Rust.
generator: python3 tools/copy_targets.py --counts 2,3,4,5 --tanks-only --output <scratch> fixtures/mage/prepared-v2/*.request.json, which skips the accepted requests that already have several targets
rerun: python3 tools/prepared_v2.py compare --output <scratch> <requests>/*.request.json, with the requests named as the generator says

criteria.comparison: full RaidSimResult except elapsedNs, lists keyed by ID
criteria.deviations: as variances at the scale of mean^2

notes: Every request Rust accepts matches the pinned Go engine on the whole result and the first-fight log: 272, those of the Paladin, Druid and Warrior tanks.

The 20 rejected requests are the Rogue (Combat with Kidney Shot, Riposte and defensive cooldowns, Subtlety with Ghostly Strike) and Mage tanks. The gate refuses a tank of a class that has not been checked against every copy of the boss swinging at it, with code several_targets_unsupported, and the exporter exports them.
